concept.title: Combinators
concept.shortdesc: A combinator describes the relationship between two elements. Put the related element’s selector on the left and the element you want to match on the right.

section.title: Descendant and sibling relationships
section.p: Use a space to select a descendant at any depth. Use > for a direct child, + for the next element sibling and ~ for any later element sibling with the same parent.
section.pre: <chapter> <title>Setup</title> <paragraph>Install the tool.</paragraph> <paragraph>Start the tool.</paragraph> <section> <title>Options</title> <paragraph>Choose an option.</paragraph> </section> </chapter>

ul.li: chapter title selects both titles, Setup and Options, because the second one is inside a section that is inside the chapter.
chapter > title selects only Setup, the title that is a direct child of the chapter.
title + paragraph selects Install the tool. and Choose an option., the paragraphs that come right after a title.
title ~ paragraph selects all three paragraphs, because each one has a title before it among its siblings.

section.title: Column combinator
section.p: The column combinator ||, from Selectors Level 5, selects the cells of the column that a column element describes. CSSMedia finds columns and cells by the display values table-column, table-column-group and table-cell, not by element names. Columns must come before the first row. CSS gives a cell no span, so each cell takes the next column of its row.
This selects every entry in a column described by a colspec, when the stylesheet gives colspec the display value table-column and entry the value table-cell.

section.title: Reference combinators
section.p: A reference combinator, from Selectors Level 5, selects an element that is referred to by an attribute of another element.
The name between slashes is the attribute that holds the reference. The rule selects every step whose id or xml:id equals the target attribute of a note. The attribute value can start with #.
section.pre: <note target="s2">Check the cable first.</note> <step id="s1">Open the cover.</step> <step id="s2">Unplug the cable.</step>
section.p: The rule selects only the second step, Unplug the cable., because the note refers to s2.
